summary: Carl Schuster (1904–1969) was a scholar in sinology and history and archaeology. He studied at Harvard University from circa 1923 to 1930 and at the University of Vienna from circa 1930 to 1934.

Carl Shigeo Yamamoto is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia, where he studied under doctoral supervisors Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano, alongside teachers Sonam Germano, William A. Magee, and Tsering Wangchuk.

Carl Siegfried (1830–1903) worked in Indology, religious studies, and linguistics. Educated at Halle and Bonn, he later served as Professor of Sanskrit at Trinity College Dublin and held an ordinary professorship for Old Testament at the University of Jena (1875–1901).

Carl W. Ernst (born 1950) is an Indology and religious studies scholar. Educated at Stanford (A.B.) and Harvard (Ph.D.), he taught at Pomona College (1981–1992) and served as a professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (1992–2022).

Carl Wilhelm Vollgraff (1876–1967) was a scholar of linguistics and history and archaeology. After studies at Brussels, Utrecht, Göttingen, and Berlin, he served as professor of Greek language and literature at Groningen (1908–1916) and Utrecht (1917–1946).

Carlo Formichi (1871–1943) was an Indology scholar who studied under Michele Kerbaker, Paul Deussen, Hermann Oldenberg, and Georg Bühler. He served as professor of Sanskrit at the University of Pisa (1898) and Sapienza University of Rome (1914–1941).

Carlo Giussani (1840–1900) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the Scuola Normale Superiore (~1859–1863) and under Giuseppe Bardelli, Albrecht Weber (1863), and Rudolf von Roth (~1864–1865).
Carlo Jamelle Harris is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts in Philosophy at National Chengchi University under the supervision of Chen-kuo Lin (attested 2009).

Carmen Blacker (1924–2009) worked in Japanology and religious studies. Educated at SOAS, Somerville College, and Keio University, she was a lecturer in Japanese at the University of Cambridge from 1958 and served as president of the Folklore Society (1982–1984).

Carmen Dragonetti (1937–2018) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy who studied at the National University of San Marcos. She served as a professor at the University of Buenos Aires and vice director of the Instituto de Investigaciones Budistas.

Carmen Meinert is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and sinology who earned her PhD from the University of Bonn in 2001. She has held posts at the University of Hamburg (attested 2008) and Ruhr University Bochum (attested 2019).

Carol A. Breckenridge (1942–2009) was a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. She studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from circa 1967 to 1976 and later held a post at the University of Chicago.

Carol S. Anderson is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under W. S. Karunatillake and John A. Brinkman, and served as Associate Professor of Religion at Kalamazoo College (attested 2004).

Carola Roloff (born 1959) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and held posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and the University of Hamburg (guest professor 2018–2025).
Carola S. Carstens is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She held a post at Rice University from 1998 to 1999 and earned her doctorate from the University of Hamburg in 2006.
Carole M. Cusack (born 1962) is a religious studies scholar. She studied at the University of Sydney from 1988 to 1995 and held a post there in 2013.

Carole McGranahan (born 1969) is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. She studied at Colgate University and the University of Michigan (PhD 2001) before serving as Assistant Professor of Anthropology at the University of Colorado Boulder (~2001–2008).

Caroline Humphrey (born 1943) works in Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies. Educated at Cambridge and Leeds under Edmund Leach, she was a university lecturer at the University of Cambridge from 1978 to 2010.

Caroline Rhys Davids (1857–1942) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy educated at UCL under George Croom Robertson. She served as General Editor of the Pali Text Society (1907–1942) and lectured at Manchester and SOAS.

Carolyn Woodford Schmidt is a history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her PhD at Ohio State University under John C. Huntington. She held posts as a graduate teaching associate at Ohio State and visiting lecturer at Denison University.
